items.stem: Define the term 'mission statement'.
items.answer: A statement of the purpose of a business and what it does, usually describing its values and its customers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A statement of the purpose of a business and what it does, usually describing its values and its customers. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a mission statement and a vision statement.
items.answer: A mission statement describes the business's current purpose and values; a vision statement describes what it hopes to become in the future.
items.markingKey: 1 mark mission = present purpose; 1 mark vision = future aspiration. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of having a clear mission statement.
items.answer: It tells employees what the business stands for, which can motivate them and guide their decisions; and it communicates the business's values to customers and investors, which can improve its image.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Tanvir Textiles Ltd, a private limited company in Bangladesh with about 420 employees, makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Explain how a mission statement could help Tanvir Textiles to achieve its aims.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: a mission statement sets out purpose and values; shared purpose motivates employees; guides objectives and strategy; builds the image of the business with stakeholders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a mission statement sets out purpose and values. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. shared purpose motivates employees; guides objectives and strategy. [3]

items.stem: The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Café Cordillera SAS, a private limited company in Colombia with about 900 employees, roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. Explain why Café Cordillera should review its vision statement as it grows.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: the vision describes what the business wants to become; growth into Mexico may change its purpose; new stakeholders may expect different values; an out-of-date vision fails to guide decisions.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the vision describes what the business wants to become. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Café Cordillera (food and drink retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. growth into Mexico may change its purpose; new stakeholders may expect different values. [3]

items.stem: Based in Kingston, Sunrise Juices Ltd (private limited company) makes fresh fruit juices sold to supermarkets and hotels. The business has around 60 employees. A new supermarket chain wants to stock its juices if it can supply larger quantities. Evaluate the importance of a mission statement to the success of Sunrise Juices.
items.answer: For: provides direction; motivates staff; communicates values. Against: often vague; success depends on strategy and implementation; stakeholders may be cynical. Judgement: for Sunrise Juices it depends mainly on whether it is backed by actions, and also on how well it is communicated.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Sunrise Juices: food and drink manufacturing, about 60 employees, private limited company in Jamaica; a new supermarket chain wants to stock its juices if it can supply larger quantities). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. provides direction; motivates staff; communicates values; arguments against, e.g. often vague; success depends on strategy and implementation; stakeholders may be cynical. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on whether it is backed by actions; how well it is communicated; the size of the business. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Sunrise Juices. [10]

items.stem: Based in Alexandria, Atlas Furniture plc (public limited company) makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores. The business has around 1,300 employees. Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Explain one disadvantage to Atlas Furniture of publishing a mission statement.
items.answer: May be vague public relations; this would be a problem for Atlas Furniture, which makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. may be vague public relations; costs time to develop; ignored if not backed by actions. 1 mark: explained in the context of Atlas Furniture (furniture manufacturing and retail). [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'SMART objectives'.
items.answer: Objectives that are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic (relevant) and Time-bound.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Objectives that are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic (relevant) and Time-bound. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why objectives should be SMART.
items.answer: Specific and measurable objectives make it clear what must be achieved and allow progress to be checked; time limits create urgency; achievable targets motivate rather than discourage staff.
items.markingKey: 1 mark clarity; 1 mark measuring progress; 1 mark motivation/time-bound. [3]

items.stem: Explain why a business might aim for profit satisficing rather than profit maximisation.
items.answer: Owners may want a balance with other goals, such as free time, social aims or good relationships with stakeholders, and maximising profit may harm reputation or staff morale.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meaning of satisficing; 1 mark reason (owner lifestyle/stakeholders/CSR). [2]

items.stem: Han River Games Co. is a private limited company based in Seoul, South Korea. It develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases and employs about 340 people. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain how SMART objectives could improve the performance of Han River Games.
items.answer: Points to develop for Han River Games: SMART: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound; clear targets focus effort; measurement allows control and corrective action; achievable targets motivate staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: SMART: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Han River Games (video game development). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. clear targets focus effort; measurement allows control and corrective action. [3]

items.stem: World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd, a private limited company in Ghana with about 450 employees, buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. Evaluate whether profit should be the main objective of Gold Coast Cocoa.
items.answer: For: profit rewards owners; provides finance for investment; measure of success. Judgement: for Gold Coast Cocoa it depends mainly on the legal structure and owners' wishes, and also on the stage of the business.

items.answer: For: clarity and focus; measurable progress; motivation. Against: rigid in fast-changing markets; not all goals are measurable; targets may cause short-termism. Judgement: for Lagos Bites it depends mainly on how quickly its market changes, and also on whether staff are involved in setting them.

items.answer: Clear targets for managers; this would help Indus Sports, which makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment.

items.stem: Explain two objectives other than profit that a business may have.
items.answer: Growth, to gain economies of scale and market power; and survival, especially for a new business or in a recession; others include market share, CSR and shareholder value.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark objective, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Define the term 'corporate social responsibility (CSR)'.
items.answer: The idea that a business should take account of its impact on society and the environment, not just on its owners.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The idea that a business should take account of its impact on society and the environment, not just on its owners. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why behaving ethically may increase a business's costs.
items.answer: Paying fair wages, buying from ethical suppliers or reducing pollution often costs more than the cheapest option.
items.markingKey: 1 mark example; 1 mark higher cost explained. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of adopting CSR.
items.answer: It improves the brand image, attracting ethically minded customers; and it helps attract and keep motivated employees who want to work for a responsible business.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Andean Coffee is a private limited company in Cusco, Peru with about 45 staff. It buys coffee beans from small farmers, roasts them and sells them to cafés. The business wants to gain Fairtrade certification. Explain the ethical issues Andean Coffee may face in its industry.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andean Coffee: business ethics concern moral principles; working conditions of employees and suppliers; environmental impact of producing roasted coffee; honesty in marketing and pricing.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: business ethics concern moral principles. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andean Coffee (food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. working conditions of employees and suppliers; environmental impact of producing roasted coffee. [3]

items.stem: Blue Lagoon Tours is a partnership in Nadi, Fiji with about 14 staff. It runs boat trips and diving courses for tourists. Most customers book in the dry season and cash is short in the wet season. Explain how adopting CSR could benefit Blue Lagoon Tours.
items.answer: Points to develop for Blue Lagoon Tours: CSR means considering the impact on society and the environment; improved reputation and sales of boat trips and diving courses; more motivated employees and easier recruitment; reduced risk of fines and boycotts.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: CSR means considering the impact on society and the environment. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Blue Lagoon Tours (tourism). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. improved reputation and sales of boat trips and diving courses; more motivated employees and easier recruitment. [3]

Judgement: for BatikPay it depends mainly on how CSR is reported and checked, and also on the business culture.

items.stem: Define the term 'corporate objectives'.

items.stem: A recession is most likely to make a business change its objective from growth to
options: market leadership
diversification
survival
maximum sales revenue
items.answer: survival

items.stem: Explain two reasons why a business might change its objectives.
items.answer: Changes in the economy, such as a recession, may make survival more important; and a change of ownership or legal structure, such as becoming a plc, brings new shareholders with different expectations.
